The entity shall establish and enforce policies governing the physical security of company-owned equipment and any media containing sensitive information at remote work locations. Employees shall be required to implement reasonable physical safeguards for laptops, mobile devices, and any physical media containing company data. This includes secure storage when not in use, prohibition of leaving devices unattended in public spaces, and proper handling and destruction of any physical documents or media containing sensitive information. The policy shall address equipment return procedures upon termination and reporting requirements for lost or stolen devices.

Implementation: Remote equipment: device encryption (FileVault), secure storage, 24hr lost device reporting.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.5 The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive i
controls.description:
CC6.5 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive information from the assets.

Before disposing of computers, drives, phones, or paper documents, ensure data cannot be recovered by others. Wipe or physically destroy storage media, shred sensitive documents, and remove company data from employee devices before reuse or disposal. Keep records of destruction for sensitive data to prove proper disposal.

Implementation: KMS cryptographic erasure. S3 lifecycle automates deletion. Retention policy defines triggers.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.5.1 Data Sanitization and Media Destruction Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal procedures for the secure sanitization and destruction of data storage media prior to disposal, reuse, or transfer. Given the remote work environment, these procedures must address both company-owned and employee-owned devices that may contain company data. Procedures shall specify approved methods for data wiping (using industry-standard tools meeting NIST 800-88 guidelines) and physical destruction requirements for media that cannot be adequately sanitized. The procedures must also address the secure disposal of paper documents containing sensitive information through shredding or secure destruction services.

Implementation: KMS for cloud data. Secure deletion for S3. NIST 800-88 guidelines.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.5.2 Asset Disposal Verification and Documentation
controls.description:
The organization shall implement a verification process to confirm that all sensitive information has been removed from assets before discontinuing logical and physical protections. This includes maintaining an inventory of assets pending disposal, documenting the chain of custody during the disposal process, and retaining destruction records for audit purposes. For the remote workforce, this process must include procedures for employees to return or certify the sanitization of company data from devices used for work purposes, including laptops, mobile devices, and removable storage media.

Implementation: KMS key deletion enables cryptographic erasure verification. CloudWatch logs track data access and deletion. S3 access logs provide disposal audit trail.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.6 The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its sys
controls.description:
CC6.6 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.

Protect your network perimeter from external threats using firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and secure remote access methods like VPNs. Monitor and restrict what can connect to your network from the internet, require extra authentication for external access, and keep security tools updated to detect new threats.

Implementation: Security groups restrict traffic. NACLs provide defense in depth. No public DB access.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.6.1 Network Perimeter Security Controls
controls.description:
The organization shall implement and maintain network perimeter security controls to protect against external threats. Given the remote work environment, this includes cloud-based firewall solutions, secure DNS filtering, and network segmentation for any cloud infrastructure. All external-facing services must be protected by appropriate security controls, with unnecessary ports and services disabled. Security configurations shall be documented and reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with current threat landscape.

Implementation: VPC + private subnets isolate infrastructure. Security groups control access.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.6.2 Secure Remote Access Management
controls.description:
The organization shall establish secure remote access mechanisms for all personnel accessing company systems. Given the fully cloud-based architecture, the organization implements a zero-trust approach where all access requires authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, regardless of network location. Access is granted based on the principle of least privilege through IAM roles, and all access sessions are logged via CloudTrail and application audit logs. This approach provides equivalent or better security than traditional VPN for a cloud-native organization.

Implementation: Zero-trust model: PropelAuth + MFA required for all access. No VPN needed - all services cloud-hosted. IAM enforces least privilege. CloudTrail + CloudWatch log all access.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.6.3 Threat Detection and Security Monitoring
controls.description:
The organization shall deploy and maintain threat detection capabilities to identify and respond to external threats. This includes intrusion detection or prevention systems, security monitoring tools, and alerting mechanisms for suspicious activities. Security tools shall be configured to detect current threat patterns and updated regularly to address emerging threats. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and significant security events shall be escalated according to established procedures.

Implementation: Security groups + CloudWatch alarms for threat detection and alerting.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.7 The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and externa
controls.description:
CC6.7 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and external users and processes.

Control and protect data when it moves outside your direct control. Use encryption for sensitive data in transit, restrict the use of removable media like USB drives, implement secure file sharing instead of email for sensitive documents, and protect mobile devices that access company data. Monitor for unauthorized data transfers.

Implementation: TLS 1.2+ for all transit. Zero-trust via PropelAuth. HTTPS-only endpoints.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.7.1 Data Transmission Encryption Standards
controls.description:
The organization shall implement and enforce encryption standards for all sensitive data transmitted across networks. This includes mandatory TLS 1.2 or higher for web communications, encrypted email protocols, and secure API connections. All remote work communications must traverse encrypted channels, and VPN or zero-trust network access shall be required for accessing internal systems from external locations.

Implementation: Lambda HTTPS-only. PropelAuth manages API keys.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.7.2 Removable Media and Data Transfer Controls
controls.description:
The organization shall establish formal controls governing external data transfers. Given the fully remote, cloud-first work environment where company data resides entirely in cloud services (AWS, PropelAuth), controls focus on securing cloud access rather than removable media. Approved secure methods shall be designated for sensitive document exchange, with appropriate access controls enforced via IAM and PropelAuth roles.

Implementation: Cloud-first architecture: all data in AWS (DocumentDB, S3). No on-premise data requiring USB transfers. PropelAuth + IAM enforce access controls. TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.7.3 Mobile Device Data Protection
controls.description:
The organization shall implement controls to protect company data accessed from remote devices. Given the small team size and remote work environment, this includes mandatory device encryption (FileVault for macOS), strong authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, and session management controls. For a company of this size, centralized mobile device management (MDM) is not required; instead, security is enforced through encryption, authentication, and access controls at the application layer.

Implementation: FileVault encryption on all macOS devices. PropelAuth enforces MFA for application access. Session timeout configured. 24-hour lost device reporting requirement in security policy.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.7.4 Unauthorized Data Transfer Monitoring
controls.description:
The organization shall implement monitoring mechanisms to detect and alert on unauthorized data transfers or anomalous data movement patterns. This includes monitoring of cloud application usage, large file transfers, and access to sensitive data repositories. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and suspected unauthorized transfers shall be investigated and documented.

Implementation: DocumentDB TLS required. CloudWatch monitors data access patterns.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.8 The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorized or malicious
controls.description:
CC6.8 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorized or malicious software.

Protect against viruses, malware, and unauthorized software installations. Deploy and maintain antivirus software, restrict who can install programs, keep all software patched and updated, scan files from external sources, and train users to recognize phishing and other attacks. Have a process to respond quickly when malware is detected.

Implementation: ECR scans containers. Dependabot scans dependencies (21 alerts). Security Hub aggregates. Code scanning via AWS not GitHub.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.8.1 Endpoint Protection and Antivirus Management
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain endpoint protection capabilities across company-managed devices. For a small remote team using macOS devices, this includes reliance on built-in macOS security features (XProtect, Gatekeeper, MRT) supplemented by cloud-based scanning of code and containers. Given the organization's size and remote work environment, endpoint protection focuses on secure device configuration, encryption, and cloud-native security tools rather than traditional enterprise endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.

Implementation: macOS XProtect/Gatekeeper provide endpoint protection. FileVault encryption enabled. ECR scans containers. Dependabot scans code dependencies. Security Hub aggregates findings.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.8.2 Software Installation Controls and Patch Management
controls.description:
The organization shall establish controls governing software installation and maintain current patch levels across all systems. Administrative privileges for software installation shall be restricted to authorized personnel only. A documented process shall exist for evaluating, approving, and deploying software updates and security patches in a timely manner. For the remote workforce, this includes ensuring personal devices used for work purposes comply with minimum security requirements.

Implementation: Dependabot auto-updates. GitHub Actions CI runs security scans.

controls.section: CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls
controls.title: CC6.8.3 Security Awareness and Malware Response Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall provide security awareness training to all personnel covering recognition of phishing attempts, social engineering tactics, and safe handling of files from external sources. A documented incident response procedure shall exist for malware detection events, including immediate containment steps, notification requirements, and remediation actions. Given the small team size, cross-training shall ensure multiple team members can execute response procedures.

Implementation: Training covers phishing, malware. IR procedure includes containment steps.

controls.title: CC7.1 The entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in t
controls.description:
CC7.1 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in the introduction of new vulnerabilities, and (2) susceptibilities to newly discovered vulnerabilities.

Continuously watch for new security weaknesses in your systems. Use standard security configurations, regularly scan for vulnerabilities, monitor for unauthorized system changes, and stay informed about new threats affecting your technology. When vulnerabilities are found, assess their risk and fix them based on severity.

Implementation: Security Hub + GuardDuty + ECR scanning. Code scanning via AWS (not GitHub).

controls.title: CC7.1.1 Security Configuration Baseline and Change Monitoring
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented security configuration baselines for all critical systems, infrastructure components, and applications. Automated monitoring mechanisms shall be implemented to detect unauthorized or unplanned configuration changes that may introduce security vulnerabilities. Given the remote work environment and small team size, cloud-native configuration management and monitoring tools shall be utilized to ensure continuous oversight without requiring dedicated on-premises infrastructure.

Implementation: Security Hub aggregates findings from multiple services.

controls.title: CC7.1.2 Vulnerability Scanning and Assessment Program
controls.description:
The organization shall implement a formal vulnerability scanning and assessment program to identify security weaknesses across all systems, applications, and infrastructure components. Regular automated vulnerability scans shall be conducted at defined intervals, with results documented, analyzed, and prioritized based on risk severity. The program shall include subscription to relevant threat intelligence feeds and security advisories pertinent to the organization's technology stack to ensure timely awareness of newly discovered vulnerabilities.

Implementation: Dependabot + Security Hub: real-time vulnerability scanning.

controls.title: CC7.2 The entity monitors system components and the operation of controls to detect anomalies that are indicative of
controls.description:
CC7.2 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity monitors system components and the operation of controls to detect anomalies that are indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors affecting the entity's ability to meet its objectives.

Set up monitoring to detect unusual activities that might indicate an attack or system problem. This includes watching for strange login patterns, unexpected file changes, unusual network traffic, or system performance issues. Use automated tools where possible and ensure alerts reach the right people quickly.

Implementation: CloudTrail: all API calls logged, validated, 90-day retention. Immutable audit trail.

controls.title: CC7.2.1 Security Monitoring Infrastructure Implementation
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a centralized security monitoring infrastructure appropriate for a small, remote-first technology company. This includes deployment of cloud-native monitoring solutions capable of aggregating logs and security events from all critical systems, including cloud infrastructure, SaaS applications, endpoints, and identity providers. Given the remote work environment, particular emphasis shall be placed on monitoring authentication systems, VPN connections, and cloud service access patterns. The monitoring infrastructure shall be configured to provide real-time visibility into system health and security posture.

Implementation: CloudTrail logs AWS API calls with integrity validation.

controls.title: CC7.2.2 Anomaly Detection and Alerting Configuration
controls.description:
The organization shall configure automated detection rules and alerting mechanisms to identify anomalies indicative of security incidents, system failures, or operational issues. Detection rules shall address authentication anomalies (failed login attempts, impossible travel scenarios, unusual access times), unauthorized configuration changes, unexpected file modifications to critical systems, abnormal network traffic patterns, and system performance degradation. Alerts shall be prioritized by severity and routed to appropriate personnel through established communication channels suitable for a remote workforce, ensuring timely response regardless of team member location.

Implementation: CloudWatch alarms on anomalous patterns.

controls.title: CC7.2.3 Monitoring Review and Response Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for the regular review of monitoring data and timely response to detected anomalies. Given the small team size, procedures shall define clear ownership for monitoring review responsibilities, establish minimum review frequencies appropriate for the organization's risk profile, and document escalation procedures for identified anomalies. The procedures shall include guidance for initial triage, investigation steps, and criteria for escalating to incident response processes. Regular review of monitoring effectiveness shall be conducted to ensure continued alignment with organizational objectives.

Implementation: Logs retained 90 days. IR procedure defines triage and escalation.

controls.title: CC7.3 The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they are security incidents.
controls.description:
CC7.3 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they are security incidents.

When security alerts occur, quickly determine if they represent real threats that could harm your operations or compromise data. Have a process to investigate events, assess their potential impact, and escalate true incidents for immediate response. Learn from events to improve detection and prevention.

Implementation: Security Hub aggregates security findings. SNS alerts on anomalies. Humadroid Incident Reporting: 0 open incidents, 100% SLA compliance. CloudTrail + VPC flow logs for evaluation.

controls.title: CC7.3.1 Security Event Triage and Classification Procedure
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain a documented procedure for triaging and classifying security events to determine whether they constitute security incidents requiring escalation. This procedure shall define clear criteria for distinguishing between routine events, anomalies, and confirmed security incidents. Given the remote work environment and small team size, the procedure shall include defined severity levels, classification criteria, and designated personnel responsible for initial triage decisions. The procedure shall be accessible to all team members and reviewed annually.

Implementation: IR procedure: severity levels, classification criteria, triage responsibilities.

controls.title: CC7.3.2 Security Event Investigation and Escalation Process
controls.description:
The organization shall implement a formal process for investigating security events and escalating confirmed incidents. This process shall include defined investigation steps, impact assessment criteria, escalation thresholds, and communication protocols appropriate for a distributed remote team. The process shall specify timeframes for initial assessment, define escalation paths, and document how lessons learned from investigated events are captured and used to improve detection and prevention capabilities.

Implementation: SNS topics for alerting. CloudWatch alarms with SNS actions.

controls.title: CC7.4 The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident response program.
controls.description:
CC7.4 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident response program.

Establish a comprehensive incident response program that activates when security incidents occur. Clearly assign roles and responsibilities - everyone should know their part when an incident strikes, including when to bring in external help. First, work to understand the nature and severity of the incident to determine the right response strategy and timeframe. Implement containment procedures to stop active threats from spreading or causing more damage. Deploy mitigation techniques to reduce ongoing impact while you work on permanent fixes. Execute remediation to close vulnerabilities and remove unauthorized access. Restore normal operations safely, ensuring threats are fully eliminated before bringing systems back online. Develop communication protocols for timely updates to affected parties, management, customers, and regulators as required. Document all actions taken during incident response. Periodically evaluate your response effectiveness and update procedures based on lessons learned. Review incident patterns to identify systemic issues needing attention. The goal is coordinated, effective response that minimizes damage and prevents recurrence.

Implementation: IR procedure: roles, escalation, containment, remediation. Humadroid Incident Reporting: 0 open incidents, 0 SLA at risk, 100% SLA compliance. Security Hub for threat detection.

controls.title: CC7.4.1 Incident Response Program Documentation
controls.description:
Establish and maintain a formal incident response program that defines the organization's approach to handling security incidents. The program shall include clear definitions of what constitutes a security incident, severity classification criteria, escalation thresholds, and response timeframes appropriate to each severity level. Given the small team size, the program should be streamlined yet comprehensive, with clear decision trees that enable rapid response without bureaucratic delays. The documentation must be readily accessible to all team members and reviewed annually or following significant incidents.

Implementation: IR procedure: severity classification, escalation thresholds, response timeframes.

controls.title: CC7.4.2 Incident Response Roles and Responsibilities
controls.description:
Define and assign incident response roles and responsibilities across the organization, accounting for the remote work environment and small team structure. Designate primary and backup incident commanders, establish clear communication chains, and document criteria for engaging external resources such as legal counsel, forensic specialists, or law enforcement. Ensure all team members understand their specific responsibilities during an incident and maintain current contact information for all internal and external parties who may need to be engaged during incident response.

Implementation: CEO as incident commander. Org structure defines escalation. IR procedure documents roles and external engagement criteria.

controls.title: CC7.4.3 Incident Containment, Mitigation, and Remediation Procedures
controls.description:
Establish documented procedures for containing, mitigating, and remediating security incidents. Containment procedures shall address immediate actions to prevent incident spread, including network isolation protocols, account suspension processes, and system quarantine methods appropriate for a remote work environment. Mitigation procedures shall outline steps to reduce ongoing impact while permanent solutions are developed. Remediation procedures shall detail the process for eliminating root causes, closing vulnerabilities, removing unauthorized access, and safely restoring systems to normal operations with verification that threats have been fully eliminated.

Implementation: Containment: IAM revocation, VPC isolation. Remediation documented.

controls.title: CC7.4.4 Incident Documentation and Communication Protocols
controls.description:
Implement standardized incident documentation and communication protocols to ensure thorough recording of all incident response activities and timely notification to relevant stakeholders. Documentation requirements shall include incident timeline, actions taken, personnel involved, evidence preserved, and lessons learned. Communication protocols shall define notification requirements and timeframes for internal management, affected customers, and regulatory bodies as applicable. Establish templates and channels appropriate for remote team coordination during active incidents.

Implementation: IR templates for documentation. SNS for notifications. CloudWatch for evidence.

controls.title: CC7.4.5 Post-Incident Review and Program Improvement
controls.description:
Conduct post-incident reviews following all significant security incidents to evaluate response effectiveness and identify improvement opportunities. Reviews shall analyze incident handling performance against established procedures, identify gaps or inefficiencies, and generate actionable recommendations. Maintain records of lessons learned and track implementation of improvements to the incident response program. Periodically analyze incident patterns to identify systemic issues requiring attention beyond individual incident remediation.

Implementation: Post-incident review process. Lessons learned tracked in board meetings.

controls.title: CC7.5 The entity identifies, develops, and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.
controls.description:
CC7.5 (CC7 - System Operations): The entity identifies, develops, and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.

Plan how to restore operations after a security incident. This includes rebuilding compromised systems, restoring data from backups, implementing additional controls to prevent recurrence, and verifying that systems are clean before returning to production. Test your recovery procedures regularly to ensure they work when needed.

Implementation: CloudWatch, GuardDuty, Lambda for monitoring, detection, response.

controls.title: CC7.5.1 Security Incident Recovery Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented procedures for recovering from identified security incidents. These procedures shall address system restoration priorities, data recovery from backups, verification of system integrity prior to returning to production, and implementation of additional controls to prevent incident recurrence. Given the remote work environment, procedures shall include specific guidance for recovering both cloud-based infrastructure and remote endpoint systems.

Implementation: BCP documents recovery for security incidents.

controls.title: CC7.5.2 Recovery Procedure Testing and Validation
controls.description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing of incident recovery procedures to validate their effectiveness and ensure operational readiness. Testing shall occur at least annually and following significant changes to systems or infrastructure. Test results shall be documented, including any identified gaps or improvements, and procedures shall be updated accordingly. For a small remote team, tabletop exercises and targeted recovery drills are acceptable testing methods.

Implementation: Q1 2025 BCP test (Feb 4, 2026) included incident recovery procedures. DocumentDB PITR enables rapid data recovery. Annual testing per BCP schedule.

controls.title: CC8.1 The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains system com
controls.description:
CC8.1 (CC8 - Change Management): The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains system components that are consistent with defined system security and availability objectives.

Implement a comprehensive change management process covering the entire system lifecycle. Require proper authorization before any changes begin - someone with appropriate authority must approve based on risk and impact. Design and develop changes securely, considering security requirements from the start. Document all changes thoroughly so others can understand and maintain them. Track changes through the entire process to prevent unauthorized modifications from slipping through. Configure software using secure baselines and monitor for deviations. Test all changes before production deployment - including unit testing, integration testing, security testing, and user acceptance testing. Obtain final approval before implementation, ensuring stakeholders understand and accept any risks. Deploy changes in a controlled manner with proper segregation of duties - developers shouldn't push their own code to production. Identify which objectives are affected by each change and verify the system still meets them. Include changes needed to remediate security incidents in your process. Maintain baseline configurations of all systems. Have emergency change procedures for critical fixes that still maintain appropriate controls. Manage patches systematically - evaluate, test, and deploy security updates promptly based on criticality.

Implementation: GitHub branch protection: PR review required. CloudFormation: consistent deploys.

controls.title: CC8.1.1 Change Management Authorization and Documentation
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain a formal change management process requiring documented authorization before any system changes commence. All changes must be logged with appropriate details including requestor, approver, risk assessment, and business justification. Given the small team size, a designated individual with appropriate authority must approve changes based on documented risk and impact assessment. Emergency change procedures shall be established for critical fixes while maintaining appropriate controls and retrospective documentation.

Implementation: CloudFormation IaC. Version-controlled deployments.

controls.title: CC8.1.2 Secure Development and Testing Practices
controls.description:
The organization shall implement secure development practices ensuring security requirements are considered from the design phase. All changes must undergo appropriate testing before production deployment, including functional testing and security review proportionate to the change scope. Given the small team, testing responsibilities shall be clearly defined with documented results. Secure baseline configurations shall be established and maintained for all system components, with monitoring for unauthorized deviations.

Implementation: Branch protection: PR approval before merge.

controls.title: CC8.1.3 Controlled Deployment and Segregation of Duties
controls.description:
The organization shall implement controlled deployment procedures ensuring changes are moved to production in a systematic manner. Appropriate segregation of duties shall be maintained where feasible given team size—at minimum, requiring peer review or secondary approval before production deployment. Final stakeholder approval must be obtained before implementation, with documented acceptance of any residual risks. Patch management procedures shall ensure security updates are evaluated, tested, and deployed promptly based on criticality assessment.

Implementation: Change policy defines approval workflows and documentation.

controls.title: CC9.1 The entity identifies, selects, and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential busin
controls.description:
CC9.1 (CC9 - Risk Mitigation): The entity identifies, selects, and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential business disruptions.

Plan for events that could disrupt your business operations - from ransomware attacks to natural disasters. Identify critical systems and data, develop backup and recovery procedures, establish alternate work arrangements, and consider insurance coverage. Test your continuity plans regularly and update them as your business changes.

Implementation: BCP with RTO/RPO. Humadroid BCP dashboard: 8 processes, 7 critical, 8 active plans. DocumentDB: multi-AZ, automated backups.

controls.title: CC9.1.1 Business Impact Analysis and Critical Asset Identification
controls.description:
The organization shall conduct and maintain a formal business impact analysis to identify critical systems, applications, and data essential to business operations. This analysis must document recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for each critical asset, prioritize systems based on business criticality, and identify dependencies between systems. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to cloud-based systems, collaboration tools, and remote access infrastructure that enable distributed operations.

Implementation: BCP: critical systems identified, RTO/RPO defined. Humadroid: AWS Infrastructure (RTO 2hrs), Customer Data Pipeline (RTO 4hrs), MongoDB (RTO 4hrs).

controls.title: CC9.1.2 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Planning
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans that address potential disruptions including cybersecurity incidents, natural disasters, and service provider outages. Plans must include data backup and recovery procedures, alternate work arrangements suitable for the existing remote workforce, communication protocols for team coordination during incidents, and defined roles and responsibilities. Plans shall be reviewed annually and updated when significant business changes occur.

Implementation: DocumentDB multi-AZ: geographic redundancy. Humadroid BCP: 8 active plans with 0 overdue exercises.

controls.title: CC9.1.3 Continuity Plan Testing and Validation
controls.description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing of business continuity and disaster recovery plans to validate their effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. Testing activities shall include backup restoration verification, recovery procedure walkthroughs, and communication protocol exercises. Test results must be documented, and identified deficiencies shall be remediated in a timely manner. Given the organization's size, tabletop exercises and targeted recovery tests are acceptable testing methods.

Implementation: Q1 2025 BCP test completed Feb 4, 2026: Full Systems recovery from backups using IaC. Status: Completed. Success Rate: 100%. Result: System recovered successfully.

controls.title: CC9.2 The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.
controls.description:
CC9.2 (CC9 - Risk Mitigation): The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.

Understand and manage the security risks from third parties who have access to your systems or data. Evaluate vendor security before engagement, include security requirements in contracts, monitor vendor compliance, and have contingency plans if a vendor fails. Pay special attention to vendors handling sensitive data or providing critical services.

Implementation: Humadroid vendor dashboard tracks 2 vendors (AWS and PropelAuth) with risk tier assignments and assessment status.

controls.title: CC9.2.1 Vendor Risk Assessment and Due Diligence
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for evaluating the security posture of vendors and business partners prior to engagement. This includes conducting security assessments proportionate to the risk level of the services provided, reviewing vendor security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001), evaluating their data handling practices, and documenting risk acceptance decisions. For a small remote team, this process should be streamlined yet thorough, focusing on vendors with access to sensitive data or critical systems.

Implementation: AWS vendor assessment includes SOC 2 Type II compliance verification. Risk Tier: Critical. Assessment questionnaire completed.

controls.title: CC9.2.2 Vendor Contractual Security Requirements
controls.description:
The organization shall ensure that all vendor and business partner agreements include appropriate security requirements, data protection obligations, and compliance provisions. Contracts must address confidentiality obligations, data handling and return/destruction requirements, security incident notification procedures, right to audit provisions, and termination procedures. Given the organization's size, standard security addendum templates should be developed for efficient contract management.

Implementation: DPA: confidentiality, breach notification, audit rights, termination procedures.

controls.title: CC9.2.3 Ongoing Vendor Monitoring and Contingency Planning
controls.description:
The organization shall implement procedures for ongoing monitoring of vendor compliance with security requirements and maintain contingency plans for critical vendor relationships. This includes periodic reassessment of vendor security posture, monitoring for vendor security incidents or breaches, and documenting alternative arrangements for critical services. For a small organization, annual reviews of critical vendors and documented backup options for essential services are appropriate.

Implementation: Humadroid vendor dashboard shows recent assessments (AWS and PropelAuth - both 2 months ago). BCP addresses vendor contingency.

controls.title: P1.1 The entity provides notice to data subjects about its privacy practices to meet the entity's objectives relate
controls.description:
P1.1 (P1 - Privacy Notice): The entity provides notice to data subjects about its privacy practices to meet the entity's objectives related to privacy.

Tell people what personal information you collect, why you collect it, how you use it, who you share it with, and what rights they have. Keep your privacy notice current, easy to find, and written in plain language. Update and redistribute it when your practices change significantly.

Implementation: Privacy notice: collection, use, sharing, rights, contact info.

controls.title: P1.1.1 Privacy Notice Development and Publication
controls.description:
The organization shall develop and maintain a comprehensive privacy notice that clearly articulates: (a) categories of personal information collected, (b) purposes for collection and use, (c) third parties with whom information is shared, (d) data subject rights and how to exercise them, and (e) contact information for privacy inquiries. The notice shall be written in plain, accessible language appropriate for the intended audience and published in a readily accessible location on company websites and applications.

Implementation: Notice: data categories, purposes, recipients, rights.

controls.title: P1.1.2 Privacy Notice Update and Distribution Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and follow procedures for reviewing, updating, and redistributing the privacy notice when privacy practices change materially. This includes: (a) defining triggers that necessitate privacy notice updates, (b) establishing a review cadence (at minimum annually), (c) documenting the approval process for notice changes, and (d) implementing mechanisms to notify affected data subjects of significant changes to privacy practices.

Implementation: Annual review. Update triggers defined. Notification procedures.

controls.title: P2.1 The entity communicates choices available regarding the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal o
controls.description:
P2.1 (P2 - Privacy Choice and Consent): The entity communicates choices available regarding the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information to the data subjects and the consequences, if any, of each choice.

Give people meaningful choices about their personal information and get appropriate consent. Explain what happens if they opt in or out, obtain explicit consent for sensitive data, and document consent decisions. Respect people's choices and only use data as they've agreed.

Implementation: Privacy choices documented. Consequences explained.

controls.title: P2.1.1 Privacy Choice Communication Framework
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal framework for communicating privacy choices to data subjects. This framework must clearly articulate the options available regarding the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information. Communications shall be presented in clear, accessible language and made available through appropriate channels including the company website, application interfaces, and direct communications. The framework must specify the consequences of each choice, enabling data subjects to make informed decisions about their personal information.

Implementation: Opt-out mechanisms explained. Clear language.

controls.title: P2.1.2 Consent Management and Documentation
controls.description:
The organization shall implement procedures for obtaining, recording, and managing consent from data subjects. Explicit consent must be obtained for the processing of sensitive personal information. All consent decisions shall be documented with sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance, including the date, method of consent, scope of consent, and the specific choices made by the data subject. The organization must maintain mechanisms to honor data subject choices and ensure personal information is processed only in accordance with the consent provided.

Implementation: Retention periods in policy.

controls.title: P3.1 Personal information is collected consistent with the entity's objectives related to privacy.
controls.description:
P3.1 (P3 - Privacy Collection): Personal information is collected consistent with the entity's objectives related to privacy.

Only collect personal information you actually need for stated purposes. Use fair and legal collection methods, be transparent about what you're collecting, and don't collect excessive information "just in case." When collecting from third parties, ensure they had the right to share it.

Implementation: Collection limited to stated purposes.

controls.title: P3.1.1 Data Collection Purpose Documentation
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain formal documentation that clearly defines the specific purposes for which personal information is collected. This documentation must articulate the business necessity for each category of personal data collected, ensuring alignment with stated organizational objectives and privacy commitments. The documentation shall be reviewed annually or when significant changes occur to data collection practices.

Implementation: Data categories defined.

controls.title: P3.1.2 Data Minimization and Collection Controls
controls.description:
The organization shall implement controls to ensure that only personal information necessary for stated purposes is collected. Collection methods must be lawful, fair, and transparent. When personal information is obtained from third-party sources, the organization shall verify that such third parties had appropriate authorization to share the information and that the data was collected in compliance with applicable privacy requirements.

Implementation: Classification governs handling.

controls.title: P3.2 For personal information requiring explicit consent, the entity communicates the need for such consent, as wel
controls.description:
P3.2 (P3 - Privacy Collection): For personal information requiring explicit consent, the entity communicates the need for such consent, as well as the consequences of a failure to provide consent for the request, and obtains the consent prior to the collection of the information.

When explicit consent is required (especially for sensitive data), clearly explain why and what happens if consent is denied. Make the consent process obvious and unambiguous, and keep records proving consent was obtained before collecting or using the information.

Implementation: Explicit consent for sensitive data.

controls.title: P3.2.1 Explicit Consent Communication and Documentation Framework
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal framework for communicating explicit consent requirements to data subjects. This framework must clearly articulate the specific purposes for which personal information is being collected, the categories of sensitive data involved, and the consequences of declining to provide consent. All consent communications shall be documented in clear, unambiguous language appropriate for the intended audience, and shall be reviewed periodically to ensure continued accuracy and compliance with applicable regulations.

Implementation: Consent requirements explained.

controls.title: P3.2.2 Consent Collection and Verification Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall implement formal procedures to obtain and verify explicit consent prior to the collection or processing of personal information requiring such consent. These procedures must ensure that consent is obtained through clear, affirmative action by the data subject, that consent records are timestamped and securely stored, and that no collection or processing activities commence until valid consent has been confirmed. The organization shall maintain auditable records demonstrating that consent was obtained before any data collection occurred.

Implementation: DPA includes consent provisions.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.1 Personal information is limited to that which is relevant and necessary to accomplish the entity's objectives
controls.description:
P4.1 (P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal): Personal information is limited to that which is relevant and necessary to accomplish the entity's objectives related to privacy.

Only use personal information for the purposes you told people about when collecting it. Don't repurpose data for unrelated uses without getting new consent. Implement controls to prevent unauthorized secondary uses of personal information.

Implementation: Data minimization principles applied.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.1.1 Purpose Limitation Documentation and Enforcement
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain formal documentation specifying the permitted purposes for each category of personal information collected. This documentation must align with privacy notices provided to data subjects at the time of collection. Technical and administrative controls shall be implemented to prevent the use of personal information for purposes beyond those originally disclosed. Any proposed new use of existing personal information requires documented approval through a formal review process that includes assessment of consent requirements.

Implementation: Purpose limitation enforced.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.1.2 Data Minimization and Relevance Assessment
controls.description:
The organization shall implement procedures to ensure personal information collection is limited to data elements that are directly relevant and necessary to accomplish stated business objectives. Prior to collecting new categories of personal information or expanding existing collection practices, a documented assessment must be completed justifying the necessity of each data element. Periodic reviews shall be conducted to identify and eliminate collection of personal information that is no longer necessary for stated purposes.

Implementation: Classification by sensitivity.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.2 Personal information is retained for the period necessary to fulfill the stated purposes unless a longer reten
controls.description:
P4.2 (P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal): Personal information is retained for the period necessary to fulfill the stated purposes unless a longer retention period is required by law or regulation or is needed to protect the entity's legal rights.

Keep personal information only as long as necessary for the stated purpose or as required by law. Implement retention schedules, regularly purge outdated information, and protect stored personal data from unauthorized access or accidental deletion while it's being retained.

Implementation: Retention periods per business and legal requirements.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.2.1 Retention Schedule Implementation
controls.description:
Define and enforce retention periods for each category of personal information based on business and legal requirements.

Implementation: Periods aligned with legal basis.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.2.2 Automated Retention Management
controls.description:
Implement automated processes to flag or delete personal information when retention periods expire.

Implementation: S3 lifecycle policies automate object expiration. DocumentDB backup retention (7 days) enforces data lifecycle. Retention periods defined in policy.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.2.3 Retention Exception Management
controls.description:
Manage exceptions including legal holds, ongoing services, and consent extensions.

Implementation: EventBridge schedules enforcement.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.3 Personal information is disposed of in a manner that renders the information unreadable, unusable, and unrecov
controls.description:
P4.3 (P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal): Personal information is disposed of in a manner that renders the information unreadable, unusable, and unrecoverable.

When personal information is no longer needed, dispose of it securely to prevent unauthorized recovery. This includes secure deletion of electronic records, shredding of paper documents, and ensuring backup copies are also destroyed. Honor deletion requests from data subjects promptly.

Implementation: Secure disposal: crypto erasure, secure deletion.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.3.1 Disposal Triggering and Scheduling
controls.description:
Identify personal information ready for disposal and schedule secure destruction according to retention policies.

Implementation: Disposal methods by data type.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.3.2 Secure Deletion Methods
controls.description:
Use appropriate deletion methods ensuring personal information cannot be recovered from any storage medium.

Implementation: KMS enables cryptographic erasure.

controls.section: P4 - Privacy Use, Retention, and Disposal
controls.title: P4.3.3 Deletion Request Processing
controls.description:
Process data subject deletion requests within legal timeframes. Notify third parties as required.

Implementation: Deletion requests processed per privacy notice procedures. KMS cryptographic erasure for secure deletion. CloudWatch logs track deletion activities.

controls.title: P5.1 Data subjects are provided with access to their personal information upon request.
controls.description:
P5.1 (P5 - Privacy Access): Data subjects are provided with access to their personal information upon request.

Give people access to their own personal information when requested. Verify their identity first, provide the information in an understandable format within a reasonable time, and explain any codes or abbreviations. If you must deny access (for legal reasons), explain why.

Implementation: DSAR procedures in privacy notice and IR procedure.

controls.title: P5.1.1 Data Subject Access Request Procedure
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal procedure for receiving, processing, and responding to data subject access requests (DSARs). This procedure must include defined intake channels for receiving requests, identity verification protocols to confirm the requestor's identity before disclosing personal information, established timeframes for acknowledgment and response (typically within 30 days), and escalation paths for complex or disputed requests. Given the remote work environment, the procedure must specify secure digital methods for both receiving requests and delivering personal information to verified data subjects.

Implementation: Identity verification before disclosure. Access policy.

controls.title: P5.1.2 Personal Information Disclosure and Denial Protocols
controls.description:
The organization shall implement protocols governing the format and delivery of personal information to data subjects, as well as procedures for handling access denials. Personal information must be provided in a clear, understandable format with explanations of any codes, abbreviations, or technical terminology used. When access must be denied in whole or in part due to legal restrictions, regulatory requirements, or other legitimate grounds, the organization must document the basis for denial and communicate the reason to the data subject in writing. All disclosures and denials must be logged and retained for audit purposes.

Implementation: Disclosure protocols. Denial basis documented.

controls.title: P5.2 Data subjects are able to have their personal information corrected based on their requests.
controls.description:
P5.2 (P5 - Privacy Access): Data subjects are able to have their personal information corrected based on their requests.

Allow people to correct errors in their personal information and update outdated data. Make the correction process straightforward, investigate disputed information, and notify third parties who received the incorrect data. If you deny a correction request, explain why and offer an appeals process.

Implementation: Correction rights in privacy notice. Update procedures.

controls.title: P5.2.1 Personal Information Correction Request Process
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process enabling data subjects to request corrections to their personal information. This process must include a clearly documented procedure accessible to all data subjects, a designated point of contact or submission mechanism for correction requests, defined timelines for acknowledgment and resolution of requests, and a systematic approach to investigating disputed information. Given the organization's remote work environment, the process shall be fully digital and accessible through appropriate channels.

Implementation: Correction process. Security policy for handling.

controls.title: P5.2.2 Third-Party Notification and Denial Appeals Process
controls.description:
The organization shall implement procedures to notify third parties who have received personal information when corrections are made to that data. Additionally, the organization must establish a formal appeals process for instances where correction requests are denied. This includes maintaining records of third parties who have received personal data, documented notification procedures when corrections occur, clear communication to data subjects explaining denial rationale, and a defined appeals mechanism with appropriate escalation paths.

Implementation: Third-party notification. Risk assessment for tracking.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.1 Personal information is disclosed to third parties only for the purposes identified in the notice and with the
controls.description:
P6.1 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): Personal information is disclosed to third parties only for the purposes identified in the notice and with the implicit or explicit consent of the data subject.

Get permission before sharing personal information with third parties, unless legally required or permitted. Ensure third parties will protect the data appropriately, limit sharing to what's necessary, and maintain records of what was shared with whom and why.

Implementation: Third-party disclosure per notice. Classification governs.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.1.1 Third-Party Data Sharing Consent Management
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal procedures for obtaining and documenting consent from data subjects prior to disclosing personal information to third parties. This includes maintaining clear records of consent type (implicit or explicit), the date consent was obtained, the specific purposes for which consent was granted, and any limitations or conditions specified by the data subject. Consent mechanisms must align with the purposes identified in the organization's privacy notice.

Implementation: Consent before disclosure. Access policy.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.1.2 Third-Party Data Disclosure Records and Minimization
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain comprehensive records of all personal information disclosures to third parties, including the identity of the recipient, the categories of data shared, the purpose of disclosure, the date of disclosure, and the legal or consent basis for sharing. Data sharing shall be limited to the minimum necessary to fulfill the stated purpose. Prior to disclosure, the organization shall verify that third parties have appropriate data protection measures in place through contractual agreements or documented assurances.

Implementation: Disclosure records. Retention policy.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.2 The entity creates and retains a complete, accurate, and up-to-date record of authorized disclosures of person
controls.description:
P6.2 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity creates and retains a complete, accurate, and up-to-date record of authorized disclosures of personal information.

Keep detailed records of when you legitimately share personal information with third parties. Document what was shared, with whom, when, and under what authority. These records support accountability and help respond to data subject inquiries about information sharing.

Implementation: Disclosure logging. CloudWatch audit trail.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.2.1 Personal Information Disclosure Logging System
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal system for recording all authorized disclosures of personal information to third parties. This system must capture essential disclosure details including the categories of personal information shared, the identity of the receiving party, the date and time of disclosure, the legal or contractual basis authorizing the disclosure, and the business purpose served. Given the organization's remote work environment, this logging system must be accessible to authorized personnel regardless of location while maintaining appropriate access controls.

Implementation: Logging requirements. CloudWatch for tracking.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.2.2 Disclosure Record Retention and Retrieval
controls.description:
The organization shall implement retention practices ensuring disclosure records are maintained for the duration required by applicable regulations and contractual obligations. Records must be stored securely, protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and readily retrievable to support data subject inquiries, regulatory requests, or audit requirements. The organization shall define retention periods, secure storage mechanisms, and retrieval procedures appropriate for a small, remote technology company.

Implementation: Record retention. CloudWatch for audit.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.3 The entity records unauthorized disclosures including breaches and other incidents involving personal informat
controls.description:
P6.3 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity records unauthorized disclosures including breaches and other incidents involving personal information.

Document all privacy breaches and unauthorized disclosures, including what information was exposed, how many people were affected, how the breach occurred, and what remediation steps were taken. This supports breach notification requirements and helps prevent future incidents.

Implementation: IR procedure for breach documentation.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.3.1 Privacy Incident Documentation and Recording Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal procedures for documenting all unauthorized disclosures of personal information, including privacy breaches and security incidents. Documentation must capture essential details including: the nature and scope of information exposed, number of individuals affected, root cause analysis of how the breach occurred, timeline of discovery and response, and all remediation actions undertaken. Given the remote work environment, procedures must address incident reporting across distributed team members and ensure consistent documentation regardless of where the incident is identified.

Implementation: Incident documentation procedures in IR procedure. Security Hub aggregates findings. CloudWatch logs provide evidence trail for breach investigation.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.3.2 Privacy Breach Analysis and Remediation Tracking
controls.description:
The organization shall implement a systematic approach to analyze privacy breaches and track remediation efforts to completion. Each documented incident must include assessment of breach severity, determination of notification requirements under applicable regulations, corrective actions implemented, and preventive measures established to reduce likelihood of recurrence. For a small remote team, this includes maintaining a centralized tracking mechanism accessible to authorized personnel and conducting periodic reviews of incident trends to identify systemic issues requiring organizational attention.

Implementation: Remediation tracking. CloudWatch evidence.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.4 The entity obtains privacy commitments from vendors and other third parties who have access to personal inform
controls.description:
P6.4 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity obtains privacy commitments from vendors and other third parties who have access to personal information to protect the personal information.

Ensure vendors and partners who handle personal information on your behalf will protect it appropriately. Include privacy requirements in contracts, verify their security practices, monitor their compliance, and take action if they mishandle data. Remember, you're often still responsible even when vendors process the data.

Implementation: DPA with vendor privacy commitments. Risk assessment.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.4.1 Vendor Privacy Assessment and Due Diligence
controls.description:
Prior to engaging vendors or third parties who will have access to personal information, the organization shall conduct a privacy and security assessment. This assessment evaluates the vendor's data protection capabilities, privacy practices, security certifications, and history of data incidents. For a small remote team, this may involve reviewing vendor security documentation, SOC 2 reports, privacy policies, and conducting brief security questionnaires proportionate to the sensitivity of data being shared.

Implementation: Vendor due diligence. DPA template.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.4.2 Contractual Privacy Commitments with Third Parties
controls.description:
The organization shall ensure that all contracts with vendors and third parties who access personal information include appropriate privacy and data protection provisions. Contracts must address data handling requirements, confidentiality obligations, breach notification timelines, data return or destruction upon termination, subcontractor restrictions, and audit rights. Standard data processing agreements or addenda shall be utilized to ensure consistent privacy protections across all vendor relationships.

Implementation: Contractual provisions. Security requirements.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.4.3 Ongoing Vendor Privacy Compliance Monitoring
controls.description:
The organization shall establish procedures to monitor vendor compliance with privacy commitments on an ongoing basis. This includes periodic reviews of vendor security posture, tracking vendor certifications and attestations, documenting any privacy incidents involving vendors, and taking appropriate remediation actions when vendors fail to meet their obligations. Given the small team size, monitoring activities should be risk-based, with more frequent reviews for vendors handling sensitive personal information.

Implementation: Ongoing monitoring. Board review.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.5 The entity obtains commitments from vendors and other third parties with access to personal information to not
controls.description:
P6.5 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity obtains commitments from vendors and other third parties with access to personal information to notify the entity in the event of actual or suspected unauthorized disclosures of personal information.

Require vendors to immediately notify you of any suspected or actual data breaches involving personal information they process for you. Include notification requirements in contracts, establish clear communication channels, and test the notification process. Quick notification helps you meet your own breach reporting obligations.

Implementation: Vendor breach notification in DPA.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.5.1 Third-Party Breach Notification Contractual Requirements
controls.description:
Establish and maintain contractual provisions requiring all vendors and third parties with access to personal information to notify the organization of any suspected or actual unauthorized disclosures. Contracts must specify notification timeframes (typically within 24-72 hours of discovery), required content of notifications, designated points of contact, and escalation procedures. Given the organization's small size and remote work environment, ensure contracts clearly define communication channels that work across distributed teams.

Implementation: Notification timeframes in contracts.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.5.2 Vendor Breach Notification Communication and Testing Protocol
controls.description:
Establish clear communication channels and procedures for receiving and processing breach notifications from third parties. Define primary and backup contact methods suitable for a remote workforce, and document internal escalation procedures upon receipt of vendor breach notifications. Maintain documentation demonstrating the organization's ability to receive timely notifications and respond appropriately to meet downstream breach reporting obligations.

Implementation: CEO designated as primary breach notification contact. Incident response procedure defines escalation. DPA template specifies vendor notification requirements.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.6 The entity provides notification of breaches and incidents involving personal information to affected data sub
controls.description:
P6.6 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity provides notification of breaches and incidents involving personal information to affected data subjects, regulators, and others.

When a privacy breach occurs, promptly notify affected individuals, regulators, and other required parties according to applicable laws. Include what happened, what information was involved, what you're doing about it, and what individuals should do to protect themselves. Meet legal notification deadlines even if investigation is ongoing.

Implementation: Breach notification per applicable law.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.6.1 Privacy Breach Notification Procedures
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain documented procedures for notifying affected data subjects, regulators, and other required parties when a privacy breach occurs. Procedures must define notification timelines aligned with applicable legal requirements (e.g., GDPR 72-hour requirement, state breach notification laws), specify content requirements for notifications including description of the incident, types of personal information involved, remediation actions taken, and protective steps individuals should take. Procedures must designate responsible personnel for breach notification decisions and execution, and establish escalation paths for after-hours incidents.

Implementation: Notification procedures. Timelines. Content.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.6.2 Breach Notification Execution and Documentation
controls.description:
The organization shall execute breach notifications in accordance with established procedures and maintain comprehensive records of all notification activities. Documentation must include the date and time breach was discovered, assessment of notification requirements, actual notification dates and methods used, copies of all notifications sent, recipient lists, and any regulatory correspondence. For ongoing investigations, the organization shall issue preliminary notifications meeting legal deadlines while reserving the right to supplement with additional information as the investigation progresses.

Implementation: Documentation. Recipient tracking.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.7 The entity provides data subjects with an accounting of the personal information held and disclosure of the da
controls.description:
P6.7 (P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties): The entity provides data subjects with an accounting of the personal information held and disclosure of the data subject's personal information upon the data subject's request.

When requested, provide individuals with a list of what personal information you hold about them and who you've shared it with. Include the categories of data, sources, purposes of processing, and recipients. This transparency right helps people understand and control how their information is used.

Implementation: Data subject accounting upon request.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.7.1 Personal Information Inventory and Disclosure Request Process
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain a documented process for responding to data subject requests for an accounting of their personal information. This process must include procedures for identifying all personal information held about the requesting individual, documenting the categories of data collected, sources of the data, purposes of processing, and any third parties with whom the information has been shared. Given the organization's small size and remote work environment, this process should designate a specific individual responsible for handling such requests and establish clear timelines for response in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.

Implementation: Inventory process. Categories, sources, purposes.

controls.section: P6 - Privacy Disclosure to Third Parties
controls.title: P6.7.2 Third-Party Disclosure Tracking and Reporting
controls.description:
The organization shall maintain records of all third parties with whom personal information has been shared, enabling accurate disclosure to data subjects upon request. This includes documenting the identity of recipients, categories of data shared, purposes of disclosure, and dates of sharing. For a small remote technology company, this may involve maintaining a centralized register of data sharing agreements, vendor relationships involving personal data, and any ad-hoc disclosures. The organization must be able to compile this information in a clear, understandable format for data subjects within regulatory timeframes.

Implementation: Third-party tracking. Recipient register.

controls.title: P7.1 Personal information is accurate, complete, and relevant for the purposes for which it is used.
controls.description:
P7.1 (P7 - Privacy Quality): Personal information is accurate, complete, and relevant for the purposes for which it is used.

Keep personal information accurate and current for its intended use. Implement quality checks during collection, provide ways for people to update their information, regularly verify accuracy for critical data, and remove or update information that's no longer relevant or correct.

Implementation: Data quality: accuracy, completeness, relevance.

controls.title: P7.1.1 Personal Information Quality Controls
controls.description:
Establish and maintain formal procedures to ensure personal information collected and processed by the organization is accurate, complete, and relevant for its intended business purposes. This includes implementing validation checks at the point of data collection, defining data quality standards for critical personal information fields, and establishing clear ownership for data quality management. Given the organization's small size, designate a responsible individual to oversee data quality practices and ensure consistency across all systems handling personal information.

Implementation: Quality standards. Classification policy.

controls.title: P7.1.2 Data Subject Information Update Mechanisms
controls.description:
Implement accessible mechanisms that enable individuals to review, correct, and update their personal information held by the organization. This includes providing clear instructions on how data subjects may request corrections, establishing response timeframes for update requests, and maintaining records of all correction requests and actions taken. For a remote organization of this size, ensure these mechanisms are available through digital channels and that all team members understand the process for handling update requests.

Implementation: User update mechanisms. PropelAuth profile management.

controls.title: P7.1.3 Personal Information Accuracy Verification and Maintenance
controls.description:
Establish a periodic review process to verify the accuracy and continued relevance of personal information maintained by the organization. This includes identifying critical data sets requiring regular verification, defining review frequencies appropriate to data sensitivity and use, and implementing procedures to remove or archive information that is no longer accurate, relevant, or necessary. Document the criteria used to determine when personal information should be updated, corrected, or disposed of in accordance with retention requirements.

Implementation: S3 lifecycle policies enforce retention periods. DocumentDB backup retention (7 days) maintains data accuracy. Periodic verification per data retention policy.

controls.title: P8.1 The entity implements a process for receiving and addressing privacy-related inquiries, complaints, and disput
controls.description:
P8.1 (P8 - Privacy Monitoring and Enforcement): The entity implements a process for receiving and addressing privacy-related inquiries, complaints, and disputes.

Provide clear ways for people to ask questions or complain about privacy practices. Investigate and respond to privacy concerns promptly, document how issues were resolved, and use complaints to identify systemic problems. Regular compliance monitoring helps catch issues before they become complaints.

Implementation: Privacy inquiry and complaint handling.

controls.title: P8.1.1 Privacy Inquiry and Complaint Intake Process
controls.description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for receiving privacy-related inquiries, complaints, and disputes from data subjects and other stakeholders. This process must include clearly documented contact methods (e.g., dedicated email address, web form, or designated privacy contact), acknowledgment procedures with defined response timeframes, and initial triage protocols to categorize and prioritize incoming communications based on severity and regulatory requirements.

Implementation: Intake process. Contact methods. Acknowledgment.

controls.title: P8.1.2 Privacy Complaint Investigation and Resolution
controls.description:
The organization shall implement a structured approach for investigating and resolving privacy-related complaints and disputes. This includes assigning responsibility for investigation to appropriate personnel, conducting thorough root cause analysis, documenting investigation findings and remediation actions, communicating resolution outcomes to complainants, and maintaining comprehensive records of all complaint handling activities. The organization shall also conduct periodic reviews of complaint trends to identify systemic privacy issues requiring broader corrective action.

Implementation: Investigation. Resolution. Trend analysis.

controls.title: PI1.1 The entity obtains or generates, uses, and communicates relevant, quality information regarding the objectives
controls.description:
